**Observations from the image:**
- Close-up of a sugarcane leaf laid on a flat surface
- Prominent central yellow/pale-yellow band running longitudinally along the midrib
- Green lamina tissue on either side of the yellow midrib zone
- No brown necrosis, no knife-cut damage, no mosaic/mottling pattern, no streaks

**Matching against classes:**

- **Yellow_Leaf**: Description explicitly states "yellowing specifically of the midribs (leaf veins)" with green lamina on both sides. This is a direct match — the image shows a classic yellow midrib flanked by green leaf blade tissue.
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Would show irregular yellow-green mosaic/mottled patches alternating across the whole leaf, not a clean central yellow stripe.
- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: Would show numerous small longitudinal streaks of varying sizes across the lamina, not a single broad central band.
- Other classes (Pokkah_Boeng, Leaf_Scald, Sett_Rot, Grassy_Shoot, Brown_Spot, Yellow_Spot): No matching features visible.

The central yellow midrib with flanking green lamina is the defining visual signature of Yellow Leaf disease in sugarcane.
